author: reek
body: Builds a CDX-shaped buffer in memory and runs the buffer ceremony over it. The content hash is computed the other way round -- with the list-based `sha256` over the same bytes -- so `hash-ok` is checked against an independent digest rather than against the function under test. Flipping one content byte must turn `hash-ok` False; a good hash with a zero signature must still refuse, because a machine that cannot prove who signed it must not pretend to know.

author: reek
body: A header whose text section spans the content, magic "CDX1", the stored hash written at offset 8, and everything else zero -- including the author key and signature, which is exactly the "unsigned" case.
